audit_findings.title: FY2024 may have been wrongly discarded from the trend anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the only filed FY2024 Plan adjustment identified is a favorable $0.1 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitting FY2024 changes the log-trend estimate used to set anchor OE and could consequently change every scenario and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the Plan, we recognized a favorable adjustment of $ 0.1 million to our estimated closing costs within selling, general and administrative expenses during fiscal year 2024, and a favorable adjustment to our expected obsolescence reserve of $ 5.8 million within cost of goods sold and $ 17.2 million in costs associated with the closure of stores and distribution centers within selling, general and administrative expenses during fiscal year 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the Plan-related FY2024 adjustment was only $0.1 million, so the Plan disclosure alone does not justify discarding the entire year. However, the record does not supply reconstructed FY2024 OE or establish that no other exclusion rule applied. The possible error is therefore unresolved, and its materiality and direction cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2024 OE using the identical historical formula, document every exclusion adjustment, and rerun the log trend, anchor, scenario values and buy-below price with all other inputs unchanged.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include cash required to operate the business
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $173.1 million, equal to $1.70 per diluted share and 8.5% of the $2,031.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash that is operationally required should be removed from the equity bridge rather than added as surplus value.
audit_findings.evidence: A substantial portion of our liquidity needs arise from funding the costs of our operations, working capital, capital expenditures and debt-servicing.
audit_findings.explanation: The unavailable portion is not established, but even the extreme correction of removing the entire $173.1 million balance would reduce base value from $19.99 to approximately $18.29 per share, still above the $16.70 market price. It would reduce the buy-below price from $13.99 to approximately $12.80, while the market price is already above that threshold. The central valuation conclusion therefore would not reverse.
audit_findings.action: Determine restricted and foreign cash, minimum operating liquidity, near-term obligations and temporary working-capital balances; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The headquarters rent holiday may temporarily inflate cash-based OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed fixed payments total $240.8 million over 26 years 4 months, averaging approximately $9.1 million per year before any Denton offset
audit_findings.mechanism: The rent-free period can temporarily increase operating cash flow and OE; projecting that benefit would overstate normalized OE and its terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: After a free rent period, payments commence on November 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The rent holiday is demonstrated, but the valuation effect is not. The filed aggregate commitment provides only a scale indicator: it does not provide the annual post-November 2026 payment schedule or the occupancy cash costs that disappear when the Denton leaseback ends. Without that reconciliation, the sustainable incremental cash burden and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Plano payment schedule, including the 30% non-lease component, identify FY2025-FY2026 cash paid or accrued for both Plano and Denton, and rerun OE using the net steady-state occupancy cost.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE includes an interest-hedge benefit that had expired by the valuation date
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.5 million pre-tax FY2025 benefit, approximately $1.1 million after tax using the filed 25.6% rate, or 0.8% of $139.8 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Failure to normalize the expired hedge benefit understates forward interest expense and overstates equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The interest rate swap will mature in April 2026 and is designated as a cash flow hedge.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiration is demonstrated, but the scale is small. Even treating the approximately $1.1 million after-tax benefit as recurring and capitalizing it at the 7.5% terminal spread produces roughly $14.9 million, or $0.15 per diluted share, versus the $3.29 gap between base value and market price. Its actual influence through one historical observation in a trend anchor should be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Verify forward interest expense using the post-April 2026 unhedged floating-rate debt balance and rerun only if the model currently carries the FY2025 hedge income forward.

audit_findings.title: Hair-relaxer litigation could create an unreserved claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured or unindemnified settlement, judgment or defense cost would reduce OE or enter the equity bridge as a claim ahead of common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, numerous cases continue to be filed against beauty product manufacturers and distributors, alleging harm from chemical hair straighteners and hair relaxer products, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition, and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied evidence describes an industry and product-liability risk, not a demonstrated SBH liability. The filings report no significant loss-contingency liability and do not identify SBH-specific defendants, claims or estimated exposure. It is therefore a forward-looking contingency not presently measurable in the valuation, while remaining capable of becoming relevant if company-specific claims emerge.
audit_findings.action: Monitor court dockets and subsequent filings; establish whether SBH is a defendant, claim counts and status, self-insured retentions, policy limits and manufacturer indemnities, then quantify and rerun the bridge or OE if a probable or reasonably estimable exposure develops.
